title: Tonal Catastrophe (Mā Má Mǎ Mà)
style: chinese opera trap fusion, 95 BPM, pipa solo, erhu strings, dramatic male lead, choral backup, dynasty cinematic, hip hop drums, gong hits, traditional flute, EN/Mandarin/Vietnamese codeswitch, comedic timing, hooky chorus, horse neigh SFX
lyrics:
[Intro — pipa solo, dramatic erhu strings, foley of a horse neighing]
There are four tones in Mandarin
Plus a neutral tone
There are FOUR ways to ruin everything you say
Today we celebrate them all

[Verse 1 — male lead, slightly desperate]
I tried to say "I love my MOM" — wǒ ài wǒ mā
Dropped the tone, hit the third — wǒ ài wǒ MǍ
Now I love my HORSE, my mother's not impressed
Tone one is flat, tone three goes down then up to bless

[Pre-Chorus — choral backup]
Mā is mother, MǍ is horse
Má is hemp, mà is to CURSE
Same syllable, four meanings, four
Pick the wrong one, you get shown the door

[Chorus — full opera-trap fusion freakout]
Mā Má Mǎ Mà — the tonal catastrophe
Mom, hemp, horse, curse — what'll come out of me?
One word, four ways to ruin your day
Tonal catastrophe, learn it the right way!

[Verse 2 — escalation]
Tried to ask for "shuǐ jiǎo" — DUMPLINGS in Beijing
Said "shuì jiào" instead — that means SLEEPING
Waiter brought a pillow, the kitchen brought a smile
The tones decide your dinner, the tones decide your style

[Verse 3 — Vietnamese cameo because they have SIX tones]
Then I went to Hanoi, thought Mandarin was rough
Vietnamese has SIX tones — six! That's enough!
"Ma" can mean ghost, mother, horse, rice seedling, tomb, OR but
Six different meanings hit me like a paper cut

[Bridge — slow, philosophical]
The English speaker says "I learned Spanish, it was hard"
The English speaker arrives in Beijing, drops their guard
Realizes pitch isn't decoration, pitch IS the word
Three months later, dreaming in fourth tone, I swear

[Final Chorus]
Mā Má Mǎ Mà — the tonal catastrophe
Mom, hemp, horse, curse — what'll come out of me?
One word, four ways to ruin your day
Tonal catastrophe, learn it the right way!

[Outro — whispered, with horse SFX]
Wǒ ài wǒ mā. Not mǎ. MĀ.
[horse neighs softly]
…close enough.
